headline: Over 100,000 measles cases reported in Bangladesh in worst outbreak
summary: The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) reports a surge in confirmed and suspected cases since mid-March, triggering a nationwide vaccination campaign.
details: Bangladesh is facing its worst measles outbreak in years, with the number of confirmed and suspected cases crossing the 100,000 mark since mid-March.
According to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), 10,773 cases have been confirmed, while 89,904 people have shown symptoms of the viral disease.
The outbreak has put significant pressure on the healthcare system, with 74,184 people admitted to hospitals nationwide.
While 70,503 patients have been discharged, the virus continues to spread rapidly, with over 1,000 people seeking treatment for symptoms in a single 24-hour period recently.
The spread of the highly contagious virus gained momentum in late February and skyrocketed by mid-March, prompting the DGHS to launch a vaccination campaign.
For comparison, the World Health Organization (WHO) reported that more than 25,000 children were infected during a previous outbreak in 2005.
caption:
Over 100,000 people in Bangladesh have been hit by the worst measles outbreak in years.

Bangladesh is facing its worst measles outbreak in years, with the number of confirmed and suspected cases crossing the 100,000 mark since mid-March.

According to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), 10,773 cases have been confirmed, while 89,904 people have shown symptoms of the viral disease.

The outbreak has put significant pressure on the healthcare system, with 74,184 people admitted to hospitals nationwide.

While 70,503 patients have been discharged, the virus continues to spread rapidly, with over 1,000 people seeking treatment for symptoms in a single 24-hour period recently.

The spread of the highly contagious virus gained momentum in late February and skyrocketed by mid-March, prompting the DGHS to launch a vaccination campaign.

For comparison, the World Health Organization (WHO) reported that more than 25,000 children were infected during a previous outbreak in 2005.

headline_marked: Actor Nadia Ahmed [[watches Lionel Messi live]] in US stadium
headline: Actor Nadia Ahmed watches Lionel Messi live in US stadium
summary: The Bangladeshi actor and dancer shared her excitement after witnessing the legendary player's hat-trick during an Argentina match in the United States.
details: Actor and dancer Nadia Ahmed recently fulfilled a lifelong dream by watching Argentina play live in a stadium in the United States. She was accompanied by her husband, actor FS Nayeem, for the experience.

Nadia described the atmosphere as electric, with over 60,000 spectators filling the stadium. She noted that the energy, shouting, and celebrations were unlike anything she had ever experienced before.

Securing tickets was a challenge, as the couple had to enter a lottery system. After failing on their first attempt, they successfully secured tickets on the second try through Nadia's sister, Nandita.
The highlight of the match for Nadia was seeing Lionel Messi enter the field and witnessing him score a hat-trick. She described the feeling as indescribable and the player as a legendary star.
A lifelong supporter of Argentina, Nadia mentioned that her mother is also a fan. While her husband Nayeem supports Germany, Nadia's passion for the team has remained constant since childhood.
caption:
From a lottery for tickets to a 60,000-person crowd—actor Nadia Ahmed just watched Lionel Messi live!

Actor and dancer Nadia Ahmed recently fulfilled a lifelong dream by watching Argentina play live in a stadium in the United States. She was accompanied by her husband, actor FS Nayeem, for the experience.

Nadia described the atmosphere as electric, with over 60,000 spectators filling the stadium. She noted that the energy, shouting, and celebrations were unlike anything she had ever experienced before.

Securing tickets was a challenge, as the couple had to enter a lottery system. After failing on their first attempt, they successfully secured tickets on the second try through Nadia's sister, Nandita.

The highlight of the match for Nadia was seeing Lionel Messi enter the field and witnessing him score a hat-trick. She described the feeling as indescribable and the player as a legendary star.

A lifelong supporter of Argentina, Nadia mentioned that her mother is also a fan. While her husband Nayeem supports Germany, Nadia's passion for the team has remained constant since childhood.
